messages:
elena: ACME just filed an escalation — their embeddings p95/p99 jumped in us-west-2 around 2026-03-16T03:12Z. p95 about 0.42s -> ~1.2s, p99 ~0.98s -> ~2.7s. They say no app changes on their side.
marc: Thanks, starting triage. Any infra rollouts in that window? driver/firmware/kernel? :mag:
jess: We began a canary of CUDA driver 12.3.1 at 03:05 and widened from 03:10-03:20. GPU FW v2.1.4 targeted the same cohort ~03:08.
raj: Hitting host telemetry: queue depth and block latency increased on several wyk1 hosts right after 03:08. Kernel shows NVMe completions piling up.
tom: ACME attached request ids and traces (req=8a7f...). Some 500s and auth retry noise, but mostly timeouts on larger inputs.
elena: sample they provided:
```
2026-03-16T03:14:21Z GET /v1/embeddings 200 1.92s req=8a7f
2026-03-16T03:14:22Z GET /v1/embeddings 500 3.10s req=8a7f retry=1
```
maya: Model-level metrics look fine (KV cache hit ratio stable, GPU util steady). Host CPU shows high iowait and SCSI latency percentiles trending up — pointing at storage contention.
li: Oncall collected quick iostat/perf for wyk1-012..016: avg await jumped 0.8ms -> 7.1ms; nvme outstanding ops spiked from ~1.9k -> ~11.8k.
marc: Temporal correlation with the driver/fw rollout is strong. Could be driver NVMe path regression or FW interaction causing long completions.
sarah: This is a Dedicated customer, so SLA exposure. Need a fast mitigation and rollback plan.
jess: Mitigation thoughts (short list): drain/evacuate affected hosts; throttle host background IO; route ACME to fallback pool/region; prepare immediate driver rollback.
raj: Starting host drains for wyk1-012..016 and adjusting routing policies. ETA ~6-8 minutes to finish shift.
deploy-bot: router:update accepted for route customer:acme -> fallback:us-west-2-burst at 2026-03-16T03:29:11Z
marc: Also applied a per-customer KV-cache bypass for long inputs to reduce repeated host IO churn for ACME.
elena: Notified ACME: "We've rerouted traffic to a fallback pool and are evacuating affected hosts. Short-term mitigation in place; investigating root cause. We'll follow up with repro and ETA." :wave:
jess: Post-drain telemetry: the drained hosts' await dropped to ~1.2ms within a minute; ACME p95 returned to ~370-400ms. That confirms host-level storage contention.
maya: For deeper triage I need: dmesg and kernel logs 03:00-03:30, nvme-health counters, driver build ids, and perf stacks for completion wait. I'll schedule a synthetic NVMe stress test under the CUDA runtime.
li: Filing incident: INC-20260316-emb-latency. Owners: jess(infra), marc(runtime), raj(sre), elena(support), maya(ml).
elena: ACME acknowledged mitigation and requested ETA. I'll tell them we're targeting a validated rollback or patch within 6-12 hours and will keep a live channel open.
marc: Next technical steps: bisect driver & FW builds (canary vs pre-canary), reproduce with nvme microbench + driver, if repro confirmed prepare rollback to 12.2.x and pin FW to 2.1.3. Prepare postmortem and SLA remediation template.
jess: I've got a candidate repro hypothesis: a regression in NVMe completion path when concurrent admin/passthrough commands are issued under 12.3.1. Will validate on full host repro tomorrow.
raj: Keep routing policy in effect until we validate rollback. Also applying a cgroup IO limit (5%) for dedicated pools to reduce background noise as a stopgap.
tom: Shared a short summary with ACME CSM and scheduled a 30m sync. ACME asked for logs for compliance — Elena, please attach.
elena: Will upload iostat dumps, dmesg snippets, and the customer traces to the ticket and post a 30m update.
infra-bot: Incident INC-20260316-emb-latency created by li. Priority: P1. Timeline link: https://redwood.internal/inc/INC-20260316-emb-latency
marc: Also double-check kernel backports applied last week (CRIU/security patch on 2026-03-10) for any interaction with NVMe paths.
maya: If we need a rollback window, consider shifting heavy tenants to quantized variants where perf delta is small — reduces GPU and IO pressure during the patch.
jess: Collating artifacts: perf traces, nvme logs, driver kconfigs, repro scripts. Will attach to the incident doc.
li: Oncall will monitor 6h after mitigation; escalate to SRE lead if p99 > 2s for any customer.
elena: Closing loop for now  hosts drained, routing applied, customer updated. Keeping channel open for updates. :heart:
